Digestion enzyme is trypsin: PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol / paper 3.7 'chemically alkylated with D6-acetic anhydride, in-gel digested with trypsin (the combination of chemical alkylation and trypsin digestion generates an Arg-C-like digestion)'. D6-acetylation blocks every unmodified/monomethyl lysine, so trypsin cleaves only after R; the CS= regex states this effective Arg-C-like specificity. All four deposited MaxQuant summary.txt: 'Enzyme ArgC'; PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol 'Enzyme specificity was set to Arg-C' (a search setting, not a second digestion enzyme).

limitations: techsdrf is not installed: instrument, NCE and scan range were read from HTTP-range reads of the first 400 KB of every .raw (method text block), not from full spectra.
Individual age is not published for any patient (Tables S1-S3 give none) -> characteristics[age] = not available on all 48 patient rows.
Individual sex is not published for breast or head-and-neck patients -> not available; ovarian rows set to female by anatomical entailment (ovarian tissue), not by a per-patient statement.

Ovarian tumors OV6, OV8, OV10 are listed in Table S2 as 'Serous surface cystadenoma, NOS' with grade 3 (internally inconsistent: cystadenoma is benign). Per-patient disease follows the Table S2 row (ovarian serous tumor, MONDO:0037255), not the paper's cohort 'high-grade serous' sentence; verbatim diagnosis and grade kept in characteristics[clinical data] (review round 1 finding 1).

'Luminal A-like' and 'triple negative' are IHC surrogate subtypes (paper 3.1); 'luminal A breast carcinoma' (MONDO:0021116) is the closest MONDO term; the surrogate definition is stated in characteristics[clinical data]. No NCIT histologic-subtype term for 'luminal A-like' was used.

HNC tumor site (oropharynx) and HNC normal site (tonsil) are cohort-level statements (paper 2.1/3.1); Table S3 has no site column, so organism part is the coarser craniocervical region (UBERON:0007811) on all HNC rows (review round 2).

Ovarian normal tissue donors had other diagnoses (Table S2: leiomyoma, fibroma, endometrioid carcinoma); the sample itself is non-neoplastic ovary -> disease normal, donor diagnosis recorded only as free text in characteristics[clinical data].
Breast tumor grade and stage, HNC/OV stage, HPV status and treatment history are not published -> tumor grading not available for breast tumors; no stage/treatment columns.

Precursor tolerance (6 ppm) comes from paper/PRIDE prose; the deposited parameters.txt do not record it. The paper's '6 ppm for fragment' contradicts the deposited 'MS/MS tol. (FTMS) 20 ppm'; the deposited value is used.
Raw file names in MaxQuant summary.txt contain a space ('LuA1 N') while the deposited files are 'LuA1N.raw'; mapping is 1:1 by name and count (30 breast + 18 OC/HNC).

The heavy reference is given one source name per run (same physical mix spiked into each sample) because the build coordinate check refuses one source with 48 runs at biological replicate 'pooled'; a reviewer may prefer a single source name.

No individual-level reduction/alkylation reagent is stated, although the OC/HNC searches declare Carbamidomethyl (C) fixed; reagent columns omitted. Paper's 'chemically alkylated with D6-acetic anhydride' is a lysine acylation, captured as Acetyl:2H(3).

sdrf-tools reconcile against the live PRIDE v3 record reports MAJOR cleavage_agent_incomplete (record names Trypsin/Arg-C, only Trypsin declared). Not acted on: Arg-C appears only as the search specificity ('Enzyme specificity was set to Arg-C') and as the 'Arg-C-like' result of trypsin after lysine derivatization; no Arg-C enzyme was used, and the effective specificity is encoded by CS=(?<=R)(?!P). Against the MCP-normalized record the same tool reports only MINOR cleavage_agent_unsupported. Both outputs are recorded verbatim in validation.txt.
characteristics[sample storage] is a custom column not licensed by the declared templates (allowed by spec 'Extending Templates').
Companion dataset PXD013288 (cell lines etc.) is out of scope; this SDRF covers all 48 raw files of PXD013311.
